title: Control plane ownership & regional routing sketch
body:
Purpose
---
Working sketch to clarify service boundaries, who owns which control-plane responsibilities, and the routing rules that span regions and tiers. Intended audience: platform-engineering, serving-runtime, SRE, and product infra. Not final; collection of constraints, proposals, and open questions.

Scope and non-goals
---
- Scope: API gateway surface, orchestration layer (control-plane), region-aware routing policy, runtime adapter responsibilities (GPU pools, quantized variants, fallback logic).
- Non-goal: implementation details of kernel selection in runtime nodes (that's serving-runtime). This doc instead defines the contracts and ownership for higher-level decisions.

High-level desiderata
---
- Predictable latency SLAs per customer tier (hosted vs dedicated).
- Deterministic fallback: an app should not see unexplained model/region jumps.
- Cost-aware routing: prefer cheaper compatible variants when within quality delta.
- Clear ownership so on-call rotations have crisp escalation paths.

Component-level ownership (summary)
---
- Edge API Gateway (ingest, auth, rate-limits, initial routing decisions): owned by platform-edge (oncall: platform-edge). Responsible for request classification, enforcing quotas, and selecting initial route policy.
- Control-plane Orchestrator (route policy execution, rollout orchestration, canary/A-B rules): owned by platform-orchestration (oncall: platform-orchestration). Exposes an evaluation API for gateway to call (lightweight, <10ms target).
- Runtime Adapter Layer (adapter per runtime family: NVIDIA RTX, A100, CPU-quantized, on-prem HSM clusters): owned by serving-runtime (oncall: serving-runtime). Responsible for compatibility checks, health signals, and spin-up/teardown of instances.
- Regional Routing Service (region affinity, compliance constraints, regional capacity accounting): owned by platform-regional (oncall: platform-regional). Provides authoritative region availability and fault-domain mapping.
- Policy Store & Audit (policy JSON, rollouts history, audit trails): owned by platform-control-data (oncall: platform-control-data).

Routing decision flow (at a glance)
---
1) Gateway receives request, authenticates, attaches token metadata (customer tier, dataset tags, prompt length distribution hint).
2) Gateway queries local policy cache -> if stale beyond 15s call Orchestrator / Regional Routing Service for authoritative decision.
3) Orchestrator computes candidate routes (ordered preference list) using: region affinity, tier SLAs, cost tier, runtime compatibility.
4) Gateway attempts candidate 1; if runtime adapter responds with capacity or incompatible error, gateway retries candidate 2, etc., with exponential backoff and strict timeout budget.
5) Successful route is recorded to Policy Store for telemetry.

Routing policy primitives (proposed)
---
- region_preference: list (e.g., [us-west-2, us-east-1])
- min_latency_ms: soft threshold per tier
- acceptable_quality_delta: e.g., 2% relative scoring drop allowed for cheaper variants
- runtime_compat_tags: required features (kv_cache, quantized_int8, half_precision)
- failover_strategy: immediate, delayed, sticky (sticky preferred for session-based chat)
- capacity_reserve: boolean for dedicated customers

Adapter compatibility & fallback rules (notes)
---
- Adapter should expose a /capabilities endpoint: comma-separated tags and a numeric "compat_score" per model family.
- Orchestrator must be able to prefer adapters with same model family and quantization (preferred) and only fall back to variants with documented quality delta.
- For on-prem/private deployments, runtime adapters may advertise 'no-fallback' to prevent cross-tenant leakage; orchestrator must respect.

Multi-region considerations
---
- Region affinity: prefer same-region serving where available to minimize latency; otherwise, honor compliance tag (e.g., data-residency: eu-only).
- Cross-region fallbacks must include a controlled TTL for session data rehydration (e.g., KV-caches may be invalidated).
- Cost-aware cross-region routing: if remote region cost > 2x, only allow fallback for high-priority requests or after local timeout threshold.
- Global outage behavior: define a "degraded read-mode" where inference requests can be routed to smaller/cheaper backends with explicit header X-Inference-Degraded: true so downstream apps can surface "degraded" UX.

Operational contracts (SLO/SLA)
---
- Orchestrator API: 99.9% availability; median 95th pct <= 10ms for policy lookup in-region; cross-region lookups <= 30ms.
- Gateway-to-adapter handshake: 99.95% success within configured time budget; failover retries bounded to avoid cascading requests.
- Incident path: platform-edge -> platform-orchestration -> serving-runtime -> platform-regional (primary escalation).

Telemetry & observability (what to record)
---
- Per-request chosen-route, candidate list, latencies per step, adapter capability snapshots, cost_estimate, and quality_delta if fallback used.
- Rollout events: who changed policy, diff, and rollout id.
- Cross-region fallback frequency by tenant (to surface mis-sized regional capacity or policy misconfig).

Open questions / decisions to make
---
- Should the gateway perform the first compatibility filter (cheap) or always consult orchestrator for policy truth? Tradeoff: latency vs central reasoning. Proposal: gateway local cache + soft-filter, orchestrator authoritative.
- How granular are the capability tags? Model family + quantization + runtime feature list or free-form? Proposal: a fixed set of tags with a versioned schema (v1 tags).
- Sticky session semantics: per-customer vs per-conversation. Need product input. (see PLAT-REQ-56)
- Backpressure: if adapter signals overload, do we queue or immediate failover? Suggest immediate failover with telemetry to avoid cascading queues.

Short-term action items (next 2 sprints)
---
- (INF-3120) Define capability tag schema v0.1 — owner: serving-runtime (Marco).
- (INF-3121) Implement gateway policy cache with 15s TTL and fallback path — owner: platform-edge (Priya).
- (INF-3122) Sketch orchestrator API contract and perf targets — owner: platform-orchestration (Aisha).
- Add canary test that intentionally triggers cross-region fallback to measure UX and telemetry end-to-end.

Appendix: example policy fragment (human readable)
---
- customer_tier: dedicated
- region_preference: [ eu-west-1, eu-central-1 ]
- acceptable_quality_delta: 0.01
- failover_strategy: sticky
- runtime_compat_tags: [ "kv-cache", "fp16", "quant-int8-optional" ]
